relationship.statement: A decision tree classifies data by recursively splitting samples on feature thresholds (x <= t) that separate classes. At each node, it chooses the threshold minimizing weighted Gini impurity so child branches become as pure as possible.
assumptions: Each decision node evaluates a single axis-aligned threshold x <= t.
The dataset contains a fixed number of samples across two classes.
Impurity is measured with binary Gini impurity G = 1 - pA^2 - pB^2.

quantities.label: Split threshold t
quantities.meaning: Cutoff value on feature x sending samples left (x <= t) or right (x > t).

quantities.label: Class separation
quantities.meaning: Distance between the two class centers along feature x.

quantities.label: Feature spread
quantities.meaning: Within-class scatter of samples around each class center.

quantities.label: Total samples N
quantities.meaning: Fixed total number of labeled samples evaluated at the root node.

quantities.label: Parent Gini
quantities.meaning: Gini impurity of the combined dataset before splitting.

quantities.label: Left branch Gini
quantities.meaning: Gini impurity of samples routed to the left child (x <= t).

quantities.label: Right branch Gini
quantities.meaning: Gini impurity of samples routed to the right child (x > t).

quantities.label: Weighted split Gini
quantities.meaning: Sample-weighted average Gini impurity across both child branches.

quantities.label: Impurity reduction
quantities.meaning: Decrease in Gini impurity achieved by splitting at threshold t.

quantities.label: Split accuracy
quantities.meaning: Percentage of samples correctly classified by leaf majority votes.
